newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's president Demirel criticises Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's president Demirel criticises Islamists.

text.p: President Suleyman Demirel has criticised Islamist calls for replacing Turkey's official secularism with a system based on Islamic law, Anatolian news agency said on Friday.
"Whoever brings politics into the mosque is committing both a crime and a sin," the agency quoted Demirel as saying on Thursday night.
"It is reactionary for anyone to want to return to the Islamic law system again," he said.

Turkey ceased to be an Islamic state in the 1920s but debate over whether to introduce more religion into public life has increased since the Islamist Welfare Party came to power in coalition last year.
A former Welfare mayor was arrested last week for allegedly making a speech calling for the introduction of sharia, or Islamic law.
Demirel holds a largely symbolic post but he is widely respected as a veteran politician and the head of state.
